answer: Like a dune that only holds its shape when every grain is anchored, an agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a small refundable stake in quartz-graded collateral. New identities start with zero trust and earn reputation only through completed, peer-reviewed work; one bad act burns the stake and the reputation. A Sybil plume of a thousand fake accounts would need a thousand stakes and a thousand clean histories, so the attack costs more than any fraud it could enable, while honest agents recover their stake on good behavior.
